title: A task that runs out of time does not leave its half-built work for the next task to commit
goal: When a task runs out of its turn part way through, it stops without putting its work away, and the changed files stay in the repository for whoever starts next. The next task begins on top of somebody else's unfinished code, and when it commits, that code goes in under its name. Make the loop hand the next task a clean starting point, or hand it the leftovers on purpose with a note saying whose they are, rather than by accident.
notes:
REPRODUCED by the 2026-09-16 triage pass, from a real instance that happened today rather than a hypothetical.

At 05:18 local the runner on separate-finds-the-boxes-in-a-dark-window-too-no ran out of turn waiting for the full test suite. queue/loop.log:

  [go-loop] 03:57:59 running task separate-finds-the-boxes-in-a-dark-window-too-no
  [go-loop] 05:18:01 task separate-finds-the-boxes-in-a-dark-window-too-no runner exited 0
  [go-loop] 05:18:02 unhealthy: 1 consecutive runner failures; waiting 30s. Last error: Waiting on the full suite...

The task went back to pending and seven files stayed changed in the working tree:
  M Sources/Photonz/EditorState+Separate.swift
  M Sources/PhotonzCore/BoxSweep.swift
  M Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/BoxSweepTests.swift
  M docs/design/separate-into-layers.md
  ?? Scripts/playtest/separate-dark-window-walk.json
  ?? Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/AppWindowSeparateFixtureTests.swift
  ?? Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/app-window-2x.png

Nothing in the loop mentions them. The triage pass handled this one instance by hand, by moving that task to the very front of p2 (seq 5) so the runner who inherits the files is the one who owns them. That is a patch for today, not the fix: the next time it happens nobody will be watching.

Note the exit code. The runner exited 0, which is how a runner says it finished, and the loop still classed it a failure from the shape of its last message. So 'did the task finish' and 'did the runner exit cleanly' are already known to disagree; this task is what the loop should DO about the tree when they do.
acceptance: When a task ends without finishing, the loop notices the files it left changed and says so in the log and on the dashboard, naming the task
The next task does not silently commit them: either the leftovers are put aside, or the task that owns them is the one claimed next
A commit can no longer carry changes belonging to a different task without anybody having decided that
Shown working by ending a task part way on purpose and watching what the next one starts from

log.note: Adversarial review before building. The mock-equivalent here was the triage's hand fix (move the owning task to the front so whoever inherits the files owns them). Rejected as the shipped answer: it only works when a person is watching, it needs the task to still be open, and it still starts the next runner on a tree it did not write. Also rejected: committing leftovers to a branch (heavier, and a commit nobody asked for is its own problem) and refusing to claim a task while the tree is dirty (the loop would idle forever on one stuck file). Shortest thing that delivers the value: take a picture of the tree before each runner, stash the difference under the runner's name, hand it back to the owning task when it is claimed again.

Built: queue/bin/leftovers.mjs (snapshot/settle/list/clear), leftovers helpers in queue-lib.mjs (recordLeftovers, handLeftovers, clearLeftovers, leftoversState, wired into claimNext and aggregateState), go-loop.sh takes the snapshot in run_runner and calls settle_leftovers after every runner (task, digest, manager), one line on the dashboard hero under the sweep. queue/ is never stashed (no task owns it, every runner writes it) and neither is anything already dirty before the runner started (the user's own repo). Untracked files are listed file by file (--untracked-files=all) so a log line names Tests/Fixtures/app-window-2x.png rather than Tests.

Verified: queue/bin/leftovers-drill.sh, 18 checks across two scenarios, all passing. Scenario 1 runs the REAL go-loop.sh against a throwaway git repo and a fake runner that dirties two files and exits 0 without finalizing, exactly the 05:18 incident shape; it asserts the log names the task, one record is written, the files are stashed under the task id, the next runner's tree has none of them, the task is handed them back with the restore command, restoring gives back the bytes, the queue's own files were never stashed, and a file the user had dirtied first was untouched. Scenario 2 makes git refuse the stash (unborn HEAD) and asserts that case is louder: state 'left', the files still in the tree, the task told, the dashboard told 'stuck'. Also green: failure-drill.sh (90 checks), manager-due-drill.sh (14), churn/decision/audit-index/sweep-notes/state-poll drills, Scripts/test.sh (7597 tests). The real path was exercised on the real repo as a guaranteed no-op (snapshot then settle with nothing changed in between): no output, no stash, tree untouched.

Left rough, no task filed (below the bar): stash entries accumulate one per incident and nothing prunes them, which is harmless because the record stores the commit sha rather than stash@{n}. A record owned by a finished task, or by the digest/manager pass, never clears itself; the daily triage pass is now told to look at those and decide, rather than inventing an expiry.

The loop now snapshots the working tree before every runner and, when the runner ends, names every file it left changed, stashes them under that task's id, records it in queue/leftovers/, shows it on the dashboard hero, and hands the record back to the owning task the next time it is claimed. queue/ and anything the user had already changed are never touched; a stash git refuses is reported louder, not quieter. Shipped in queue/bin/leftovers.mjs, queue-lib.mjs, go-loop.sh and the dashboard page; drilled end to end by queue/bin/leftovers-drill.sh (18 checks, both scenarios green) plus failure-drill (90), manager-due-drill (14), the node drills and Scripts/test.sh (7597 tests). Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-16-task-leftovers.json. Commit 10b411c3, pushed.
